minutes.headline: Water commissioners accepted six-month temporary borrowing for the Massachusetts Ave main and sent back zoning and Hickory Hills positions.
minutes.summary: The commissioners heard a Mass Ave water main update, accepted minutes, and voted on temporary borrowing for the project. They discussed the proposed water supply zoning bylaw, objecting to a special permit requirement in Zone 1, and spent most of the meeting on Hickory Hills well issues, including a lawyer's four-point letter from The Woodlands and a talk with a landowners' representative. Superintendent items covered the AT&T cell tower lease and lightning damage to two Lancaster Ave wells.

public_comment.topic: A person identified as Bill Han spoke on the zoning bylaw, supporting the overall bylaw even if a special permit is required.
Representing Hickory Hills Landowners, suggested a swim dock as an alternative to the beach in the easement area.
Responded on the PFAS data, funding, and fee numbers, lake levels and monitoring of the well, and offered to send a wish list.
A consultant for hand in hand engineering spoke on the zoning bylaw changes, site plan review only in Zones 1 and 2.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of June 26th, June 10th and July 10th.
Accept the six-month temporary borrowing for the Massachusetts Ave water main project through Piper Sandler.
Motion to adjourn requested by the chair.

budget_items.topic: Temporary borrowing for Mass Ave water main
budget_items.what_was_said: Two bids were received; Piper Sandler won. The borrowing is temporary, with a bond planned once the project is done.

budget_items.topic: Legal fees on Hickory Hills correspondence
budget_items.what_was_said: The clerk and commissioners worried about paying counsel to answer the Woodlands attorney and preferred meeting directly.

budget_items.topic: Fee structure and project funding for PFAS treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion of per-user cost estimates and a state loan at zero interest, disputed with the landowners' representative.

budget_items.topic: Cost of a pipe for pump discharge below the dam
budget_items.what_was_said: Superintendent said the requested discharge pipe would cost far too much.

budget_items.topic: AT&T cell tower lease on Chase Road
budget_items.what_was_said: AT&T asked to lower the monthly rent and escalator; the board preferred putting out an RFP for the open site.

decisions.decision: The clerk will follow up with the planning board to ask for an updated draft zoning bylaw before the next meetings.
Board consensus to support the whole bylaw but not the special permit requirement in Zone 1.
Clerk and superintendent will draft a written response to the Woodlands attorney's four requests, offering an on-site meeting, for board review before sending.
John Fortune asked to send a wish list of top items for a future meeting on Hickory Hills.
The board favored putting out an RFP for the open site at the Chase Road tower rather than agreeing to AT&T's reduced rent.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners voted to accept six-month temporary borrowing for the Massachusetts Ave water main project through Piper Sandler, which won over one other bid.
The board reached consensus to support the proposed water supply zoning bylaw as a whole but not its special permit requirement in Zone 1.
The clerk and superintendent will draft a written reply to the Woodlands attorney's four requests, offering an on-site meeting, for board review before it is sent.
A landowners' representative on Hickory Hills was asked to send a wish list of top items for a future meeting.
On the Chase Road cell tower, the board favored an RFP for the open site over accepting AT&T's request for reduced rent.

why_it_matters: The temporary borrowing is the first financing step for the Mass Ave main, and a bond is planned once the project is done, so the final cost to water users depends on that later vote.

The board's objection to the Zone 1 special permit and the Hickory Hills well dispute, which includes PFAS treatment fees and legal costs, could affect what water customers pay and how land near the wells is regulated.
watch_next: An updated draft zoning bylaw, which the clerk is to request from the planning board before the next meetings.
The board's written response to the Woodlands attorney, and the Hickory Hills wish list for a future meeting.
